neighbours.label: A word inside an abbreviated journal title in a reference citation (J Am Diet Assoc, J Altern Complement Med), vs the same words in running prose
fire: Lee M. Sleep and memory. J Clin Sleep Med. 2010;6:12-8.
Brown A. Exercise in older adults. J Am Geriatr Soc. 2008;56:200-6.
Chen L. Salt intake and blood pressure. Am J Clin Nutr. 2012;95:31-9.
Garcia R. Asthma in children. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2015;135:44-50.
Patel S. Yoga for back pain. J Altern Complement Med. 2011;17:9-15.
Kim H. Fiber and heart disease. J Am Diet Assoc. 2009;109:77-82.
Nguyen T. Smoking and stroke. Stroke. 2004;35:1-6. See also J Hypertens. 2006;24:3-9.
Wilson P. Diabetes risk. Diabetes Care. 2007;30:11-6; Ann Intern Med. 2008;148:5-12.
quiet: Lee wrote a short book about sleep and memory in 2010.
Brown found that exercise helps older adults stay independent.
Chen showed that salt intake raises blood pressure in some people.
Garcia studies asthma in children at a hospital in Texas.
Patel teaches yoga to people with back pain on weekends.
Kim says fiber may protect against heart disease.
Nguyen quit smoking after his father had a stroke.
Wilson talked about diabetes risk at the town meeting.

predictions: Words and pieces inside abbreviated journal names in citations 0.4-0.8; the same topic words in prose sentences under 0.05.
notes: Card: no single token; top examples include J Altern Com|plement Med, J Am Diet Assoc, J Hyp|ert|ens, plus OCR newspaper text and URLs. Probe: J Altern Complement Med 0.777, J Am Diet Assoc 0.711; URL 0.048, prose 'diet and stroke risk' 0.017, 'higher learning' 0.002, 'global coordinates' 0.001. Only the citation strand was probed; the OCR/URL strand did not reproduce.
